meta.summary: HAZOP of the MCFC stack node (air, feed and H2 BOG inlets through the internal reformer, anode and cathode to the Cathode Out, Anode Out and Vent Out lines and the DC-Power output). The worksheet has 27 rows. Deviations covered: No/Less/More flow of air, feed and H2 BOG; steam-to-carbon, sulphur and sea-salt contamination; high and low stack pressure, including blocked outlets at BV-400/BV-410 and anode-cathode differential; high and low stack and inlet temperature; No/Less/More DC power; reverse flow from the vent / cathode outlet (row 21 corrects row 16 to match the drawing); loss of instrument air or control power; start-up sequence; external leakage; and electrolyte loss. The highest-ranked scenarios are external H2/CO leakage and blocked-outlet overpressure (RI 15, SIL 2). Main recommendations: independent high-pressure and gas-detection SIFs; an anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter; low air/fuel flow and high-high temperature trips; start-up permissives; N2 purge on shutdown; confirming LCV fail positions and that PSV-160 covers the anode; and locating Vent Out in a safe area, backed by a dispersion study.
meta.criteria: Default 5x5 risk ranking (FI / SI / RI / SIL)

rows.deviation: No Flow | Air to cathode
rows.causes: LCV-200 fails closed or air compressor trips
rows.consequences: No O2/CO2 reaches the cathode. Cell voltage collapses and the cells can reverse. Air no longer cools the stack, so local hot spots form. Fuel keeps flowing to the anode with no reaction, which creates a pressure imbalance between anode and cathode. This can break the wet seal, letting H2 cross over into the cathode and burn inside the stack, damaging it severely. Propulsion power is lost.
safeguards: BPCS control via SIC-400 of LCV-100/200/300
recommendations: Add an independent low-low air flow trip (SIL 1) that closes LCV-100 and LCV-300 and isolates the DC load
Verify LCV-200 fail-safe position and add valve position feedback

rows.deviation: Less Flow | Air to cathode
rows.causes: Air compressor degradation, fouled air intake filter, or SIC-400 / LCV-200 control fault
rows.consequences: The cathode is starved of O2/CO2 and the air does less cooling. Cell voltage drops and stack temperature rises. Local overheating speeds up electrolyte loss and corrosion, and stack life is shortened.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add low air flow alarm on FIT-110 with automatic load reduction
Add a high stack temperature trip independent of the BPCS

rows.deviation: More Flow | Air to cathode
rows.causes: LCV-200 fails open or SIC-400 control fault
rows.consequences: The stack is over-cooled and its temperature falls toward the carbonate freezing point. The electrolyte cracks and gas crosses over. Cathode pressure rises compared with the anode, so the differential across the wet seal goes up. Stack damage is possible.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high air flow alarm and low stack temperature alarm/trip
Install anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm

rows.deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: LCV-100 fails closed, natural gas compressor trip or water pump trip
rows.consequences: The anode is starved of fuel while current is still being drawn. Cells reverse and the Ni anode oxidises, causing irreversible stack damage. Propulsion power is lost.
recommendations: Add a low-low fuel flow / low cell voltage trip that disconnects the DC load
Provide automatic switchover to H2 BOG fuel within permitted load limits

rows.deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: LCV-100 fails open or SIC-400 control fault
rows.consequences: Excess endothermic reforming over-cools the stack and creates thermal gradients that can crack the cells. Anode pressure rises. Unreacted fuel is carried to the anode outlet, which can overheat downstream combustion equipment.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high feed flow alarm on FIT-100 and fuel-to-current ratio limiting in the BPCS

rows.deviation: Other than Composition | Feed (low steam-to-carbon ratio)
rows.causes: Water pump failure or wrong water/natural gas proportion in the feed
rows.consequences: Carbon deposits in the internal reformer and the anode. The catalyst deactivates and flow passages block, causing pressure rise and maldistribution. Stack damage and loss of power follow.
recommendations: Install separate water and natural gas flow measurement with steam-to-carbon ratio control and a low-ratio trip

rows.deviation: As well as Composition | Feed (sulphur / impurities)
rows.causes: Desulphurisation upstream fails or the natural gas supply is off-specification
rows.consequences: The reformer catalyst and Ni anode are poisoned. Performance degrades and stack life is shortened (economic loss).
recommendations: Provide a sulphur analyser downstream of the desulphuriser with alarm

rows.deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
rows.causes: LCV-300 fails open or a BOG surge from the cargo tanks (ship motion, heat ingress)
rows.consequences: H2 replaces reformate, so less endothermic reforming takes place and the heat balance is lost. The stack overheats and anode pressure rises. Electrolyte loss, seal damage and possible H2 leakage follow.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high H2 flow alarm and a high-high stack temperature trip that closes LCV-300
Limit the H2 BOG share of fuel in the BPCS with feed-forward on FIT-120

rows.deviation: No Flow | H2 BOG to anode
rows.causes: LCV-300 fails closed or H2 BOG compressor trip
rows.consequences: Fuel to the anode drops and power output falls. If the load is not reduced, the anode is starved locally. BOG builds up in the cargo tanks (outside this node).
safeguards: BPCS fuel flow control via SIC-400
recommendations: Implement automatic compensation by feed flow (LCV-100) and load reduction on low H2 flow

rows.deviation: More Pressure | Stack anode / cathode
rows.causes: BV-400 or BV-410 (fail-closed) closes spuriously or loses its signal/actuating air while the inlets remain open
rows.consequences: The outlet is blocked and pressure in the stack rises. The wet seals fail and hot H2/CO-rich gas is released into the machinery space. Fire or explosion and CO toxicity can cause multiple fatalities.
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
recommendations: Install stack pressure transmitters on anode and cathode with an independent high-high pressure SIF (SIL 2) that closes LCV-100/200/300 and opens BV-160
Add position feedback on BV-400 and BV-410, interlocked with the inlet valves
Verify PSV-160 sizing for the blocked-outlet case and that it protects both anode and cathode

rows.deviation: More Pressure | Anode-to-cathode differential
rows.causes: Mismatch between fuel (LCV-100/LCV-300) and air (LCV-200) flows, or uneven throttling of BV-400 against BV-410
rows.consequences: The electrolyte wet seal is broken and gas crosses over. H2/CO burns directly with air inside the stack, causing hot spots and cell or stack destruction. A fire may spread outside the stack.
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Install an anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm and a SIL 1 trip

rows.deviation: More Temperature | MCFC stack
rows.causes: Too little reforming heat sink (low feed with high H2 BOG share), excessive current draw, or low cathode air flow
rows.consequences: Stack temperature goes above the design value of about 650 °C. Carbonate evaporates and corrodes the components, seals and separator plates degrade, and gas can leak with a fire risk. Stack life is much reduced.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210, TI-200/TI-210 and TT-410 stack temperature
TE-300 / TI-300 and TE-310 / TI-310 outlet temperatures
recommendations: Add an independent high-high stack temperature trip (SIL 1) that reduces load and fuel
Add high temperature alarms on TI-300/TI-310

rows.deviation: Less Temperature | MCFC stack
rows.causes: Excess air (LCV-200 open), excess feed reforming, prolonged low load, or an uncontrolled cool-down after a trip
rows.consequences: The carbonate electrolyte solidifies (below about 490 °C). The electrolyte matrix cracks and gas crosses over on reheating. The stack is damaged permanently.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add a low stack temperature alarm and a procedure for controlled hot standby / heat-up
Consider stack electric heaters for hot standby

rows.deviation: More Power | DC output
rows.causes: Propulsion load demand above stack capability, power converter fault or short circuit
rows.consequences: Current is too high for the fuel supplied, so fuel utilisation is excessive. The anode is starved, cells reverse and overheat, and the stack is damaged. A short circuit can cause arc flash and electrical fire.
safeguards: IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current measurement and recording
recommendations: Provide current limiting in the power converter, linked to available fuel flow
Provide DC overcurrent / short-circuit protection on the DC-Power output

rows.deviation: No Power | DC output
rows.causes: DC breaker trip or load rejection by the propulsion system
rows.consequences: The cells reach open-circuit voltage and the voltage goes high. Fuel is not consumed and flows to Anode Out, and the stack cools. The ship loses propulsion power, which in confined waters can lead to collision or grounding.
safeguards: Multiple stack modules providing partial redundancy
recommendations: Implement automatic fuel cutback on load rejection
Review propulsion redundancy and emergency power against class rules

rows.deviation: Reverse Flow | Vent line into stack
rows.causes: BV-160 opens on shutdown or utility failure while stack pressure is low, letting air back in from Vent Out
rows.consequences: Air enters the anode side. A flammable H2/air mixture forms at high temperature and can explode inside the stack. The Ni anode oxidises.
recommendations: Provide an inert gas (N2) purge of the anode on shutdown
Install a check valve or flame arrester on the vent line

rows.deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power
rows.causes: Loss of instrument air or control power
rows.consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 fail closed and BV-160 fails open. Stack gas, including H2 and CO, is dumped to Vent Out. If the LCVs do not fail closed, fuel keeps flowing to the vent and a flammable cloud forms at the vent outlet. The stack also cools in an uncontrolled way.
recommendations: Confirm that LCV-100 and LCV-300 fail closed, and confirm the LCV-200 fail position
Locate Vent Out in a safe area, backed by hazardous area classification and a dispersion study
Provide a UPS for the control system

rows.deviation: Other than Operation | Stack start-up
rows.causes: H2 BOG or feed is admitted before the stack is purged or brought up to temperature, or the start-up sequence is done in the wrong order
rows.consequences: A flammable mixture forms in the stack and ducts and can explode. Thermal shock and gas crossover follow if the electrolyte is not yet molten. Multiple fatalities are possible in an enclosed machinery space.
recommendations: Implement start-up permissives (purge complete, stack temperature above electrolyte melting point) before LCV-100/LCV-300 can open
Provide written start-up/shutdown procedures and operator training

rows.deviation: Part of Composition | Stack containment (external leak)
rows.causes: Seal, gasket or flange failure at the stack or its inlet/outlet piping from thermal cycling, ship motion or corrosion
rows.consequences: Hot H2/CO-rich gas is released into the machinery space, with jet fire or explosion and CO poisoning of crew. Multiple fatalities are possible.
recommendations: Install H2 and CO gas detection in the stack enclosure with an ESD (SIL 2) that closes LCV-100/200/300
Provide a ventilated stack enclosure per the IGF Code
Set up an inspection programme for seals and flanges

rows.deviation: Less Level | Electrolyte in stack
rows.causes: Carbonate is gradually lost through evaporation, corrosion and creep over the operating life
rows.consequences: The electrolyte matrix dries out and gas crosses over. Cell voltage falls and local combustion hot spots develop.
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Trend cell voltage deviation for predictive stack replacement

rows.deviation: Reverse Flow | Vent Out / Cathode Out into stack (correction to row 16)
rows.causes: BV-160 opens (fail-open on utility loss or shutdown) or BV-410 is open while stack pressure decays after a trip, so air or exhaust flows back from Vent Out / Cathode Out into the cathode outlet line
rows.consequences: Air enters the cathode outlet line, which also carries anode exhaust routed internally from the anode to the cathode. Air can then migrate through the internal anode-to-cathode path into the anode while residual H2/CO is still present. A flammable mixture can form at about 650 °C, with internal deflagration and stack damage, and the Ni anode oxidises. (Row 16 wrongly says air enters the anode directly.)
safeguards: BV-400 / BV-410 fail-closed on utility loss
recommendations: Provide an inert gas (N2) purge of the anode and cathode on shutdown, before BV-160 vents to atmosphere
Install a check valve or flame arrester on the Vent Out line downstream of BV-160 / PSV-160
Review the shutdown sequence so the stack is not left open to Vent Out / Cathode Out while unpurged

rows.deviation: Less Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: LCV-100 partly closed or a SIC-400 control fault, natural gas compressor degradation, or water pump underperformance
rows.consequences: There is too little fuel for the current drawn, so fuel utilisation is high. The anode is starved locally, cells drop in voltage and can reverse, and the Ni anode oxidises. With less endothermic reforming, the stack temperature rises. Stack life is shortened and power output falls.
safeguards: TT-410 / SIC-400 temperature and current control
recommendations: Add a low feed flow alarm on FIT-100 with automatic current limiting through SIC-400 / IT-400

rows.deviation: Less Flow | H2 BOG to anode
rows.causes: LCV-300 partly closed, H2 BOG compressor degradation, or low boil-off from the cargo tanks
rows.consequences: Total fuel to the anode drops. If the feed does not compensate, the anode is starved locally, voltage falls and power falls. The stack is not damaged if the load is reduced.
recommendations: Add a low H2 flow alarm on FIT-120 with feed-forward compensation through LCV-100

rows.deviation: More Temperature | Feed / air / H2 BOG inlet
rows.causes: Upstream heat exchanger bypass or control failure (outside this node) gives hot inlet gas
rows.consequences: The stack inlet is overheated and thermal gradients form. Carbon can deposit at the reformer inlet from cracking of natural gas. Stack temperature rises and the stack ages faster.
safeguards: TE-100 / TI-100, TE-110 / TI-110 and TE-120 / TI-120 inlet temperature indication
TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high temperature alarms on TI-100, TI-110 and TI-120

rows.deviation: Less Pressure | Stack anode / cathode
rows.causes: PSV-160 lifts or passes, BV-160 opens spuriously (fail-open), or an external leak occurs
rows.consequences: The stack depressurises and stack gas, including H2 and CO, is released to Vent Out. The anode-cathode differential is upset and gas crosses over. Flammable or toxic gas is released at the vent outlet.
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
recommendations: Add position feedback on BV-160 with an alarm
Locate Vent Out in a safe area, confirmed by a dispersion study

rows.deviation: Less Power | DC output
rows.causes: Cell degradation, fuel or air shortfall, or loss of one or more stack modules
rows.consequences: Propulsion power is reduced. Manoeuvrability is limited in confined waters.
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Provide power management that sheds non-essential load and alarms on the bridge

rows.deviation: As well as Composition | Air to cathode (sea salt / water spray)
rows.causes: Air intake filtration fails or green water / sea spray is drawn into the air compressor intake in heavy weather
rows.consequences: Chlorides and sodium enter the cathode. The cathode and separator plates corrode faster and the carbonate electrolyte is contaminated. Cell performance drops and stack life is shortened (economic loss).
safeguards: TE-110 / TI-110 and PIT-110 / PI-110 air inlet indication
recommendations: Provide marine-grade air intake filtration (salt/coalescing filters) with differential pressure alarm
Locate the air intake away from spray zones and exhaust/vent outlets
